the most common renal lesions in type 2 diabetics were non-diabetic renal diseases (50%), non- diabetic renal disease superimposing on underlying diabetic nephro- pathology (14.5%) and isolated diabetic nephropa- thy (35.5%).
in patients with type II diabetes, non-diabetic renal diseases are more common than diabetic nephropathy.
NDRD is the main cause of renal disease in patients with type II diabetes mellitus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histopathological analysis of the spectrum of biopsy-proven glomerular lesions in type 2 diabetics.
the spectrum of biopsy-proven kidney diseases in patients with diabetes mellitus type 2 and the clinical features that can suggest the diagnosis of non-diabetic renal involvement.
the histopathological spectrum of biopsy-proven NDRD in diabetic patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in patients with type-2 DM, the diagnosis of diabetic nephropathy should be considered in all cases of nephropathy, regardless of the presence of other clinical and laboratory parameters suggestive of non-diabetic renal diseases.
NDRD may coexist with DN in type 2 DM.

in type 2 patients with diabetic nephropathy, renal biopsy should be performed in cases of hematuria, proteinuria of unknown etiology, and in the presence of other signs of non-diabetic renal diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NDRD may co-exist with DN and may be the cause of renal failure in diabetic patients.
the spectrum of biopsy-proven non-diabetic renal diseases is similar to that seen in non-diabetic individuals, and that non-diabetic renal pathology is not rare in patients with type II diabetes.
the most frequent histological pattern in type 2 diabetics was FSGS and DN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prevalence of NDRD is high in patients with type II diabetes mellitus and that the presence of FSGS in diabetic patients may indicate the coexistence of NDRD.

the presence of NDRD in type 2 patients with diabetes is more common than previously thought and that it is important to consider the possibility of a coexisting NDRD in the evaluation of diabetic patients with renal involvement.
NDRD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of renal disease in diabetic patients.
